evidence.text: Funding test. The money funds losses, not a ramp (production down 38%, deliveries down 4% QoQ), so it is likely to need either new PIF or third-party funding announced with the print, which would be dilutive at $3.5 against the $8.32 Uber and $10.65 Series C prices of April, or weaker liquidity language.

evidence.text: This is the first call since the settlement, and it must quantify the PH-ILD exit. Management said on the Q4-2025 and Q1-2026 calls that new YUTREPIA prescriptions split roughly evenly between PAH and PH-ILD, and on the Q2 call it reaffirmed '>$1B net revenue in 2027'. Liquidia's own 13 Oct release lists 'the impact of ceasing PH-ILD promotion and sales' as uncertain and gives no figure. A Q4/2027 outlook that removes about half of new-patient flow, and withdraws or rebases the $1B ambition, is the line this print turns on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has never been a formal guide. The two outlook-type shocks were the 2026-09-30 ruling (-57% in a day, $70.69 to $30.26) and the 2026-10-13 settlement (+26% to +40% intraday). The stock is very sensitive to the PH-ILD question.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is still 47% below its high. But it has rallied about 42% since the settlement day (about $33.9 to $48.1) and 8% on the eve of the print, with no new company document since 14 Oct (EDGAR shows only Form 4s). The rally is therefore pricing a benign PAH-only run-rate, or continued off-label PH-ILD use, that management has not confirmed. If the market had priced a roughly 50% loss of new-patient flow, the stock would not have re-rated above the post-settlement level into the print. Sized down for the 22% short float, and net of the PAH half, which grew sales 31% q/q in Q3.
evidence.independence: The roughly even split is from third-party call summaries (MarketBeat/Barchart Q1-2026 highlights, snippet only: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/liquidia-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-05-11/). No analyst or the company has published a PH-ILD revenue share; IBTimes (2026-10-15) states 'Liquidia has not disclosed how much of its recent sales came from PH-ILD patients' (https://www.ibtimes.com.au/liquidia-united-therapeutics-yutrepia-settlement-1876695). Countervailing: the settlement 8-K bars promotion 'immediately', and the release of claims waits on FDA approval of the label change, so Q4 PH-ILD sales may continue for a while.

The money buys continued PAH commercialisation, not a ramp, and leaves about $160m before Q4 operating cash flow.
